title: 6.0001 Introduction to Computer Science and Programming in Python
description: 6.0001 Introduction to Computer Science and Programming in Python is intended for students with little or no programming experience. It aims to provide students with an understanding of the role computation can play in solving problems and to help students, regardless of their major, feel justifiably confident of their ability to write small programs that allow them to accomplish useful goals. The class will use the Python 3.5 programming language.

schedule.topic: String Manipulation, Guess and Check, Approximations, Bisection

requiredMaterials: Guttag, John. Introduction to Computation and Programming Using Python: With Application to Understanding Data, Second Edition. MIT Press, 2016. ISBN: 9780262529624.

policies.name: Lecture attendance
policies.text: Students are expected to regularly attend lectures.

policies.name: Recitation attendance
policies.text: Recitation attendance is encouraged but not required.

policies.name: Quiz materials
policies.text: Both quizzes are closed-book. One page of notes is allowed for the first quiz and two for the second; pages must be letter-sized, double-sided, handwritten or typed.

policies.name: Extensions and dropped problem sets
policies.text: No extensions are granted; late days are available, and at most two problem-set grades may be rolled into the final quiz score.

policies.name: Late days
policies.text: Late days must be used as whole days. Staff track remaining late days; additional late work beyond available late days will not be accepted.

warnings: Historical Fall 2016 syllabus. It explicitly uses Python 3.5; review and update this for a current institution before publishing.
No unambiguous term start or end dates, or calendar dates for individual sessions, are supplied. Dates have been omitted.

Grading weights are omitted: Grading Policy lists 30% problem sets, 10% finger exercises, 20% midterm quiz and 40% final quiz, but Rolling Over Problem Sets permits transferring up to two problem-set weights to the final quiz. Configure this conditional policy manually; existing course weights are not replaced.
Late Days contains a longer accumulation policy; consult the complete syllabus before configuring deadlines. The extracted policies are a review aid, not the entire syllabus.
Quizzes and finger exercises are not supplied by OCW. This bundle contains the syllabus and one lecture excerpt, not the complete course or its textbook.
